## Why This Is Asked
Shows ability to architect supply chain security from CI to runtime with policy enforcement.

## Key Concepts
- Image signing (Sigstore/cosign)
- Admission control (Kyverno or Gatekeeper)
- Provenance and trusted registries
- CI/CD integration and audits
- Remediation strategies

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-signed-images
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  rules:
  - name: verify-signature
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment","StatefulSet"]
    validate:
      message: "Image must be signed with cosign provenance"
      pattern:
        spec.template.spec.containers[].image: "?*"
```

- How would you handle auto-rotation of signing keys?
- How would you test this in a staging cluster?

```javascript
  name: enforce-restricted-ps
```

```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (conceptual)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8spodsecurity
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8SPodSecurity
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package k8spodsecurity
      # policy consolidated in real template
```
```yaml
# Constraint (conceptual)
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8SPodSecurity
spec:
  match:
    kinds:
      - apiGroups: ["apps"]
        kinds: ["Deployment"]
  parameters:
    allowList:
      - registry.example.com/*
```

## Why This Is Asked

- Sigstore Cosign sign-blob attest and verify-blob
- Model provenance and SBOM

## Code Example
```bash
# Sign a model blob and create an attestation
cosign sign-blob -key cosign.key models/model-v1.bin
cosign attest -key cosign.key --predicate predicate.json models/model-v1.bin
cosign verify-blob -key cosign.pub models/model-v1.bin
```

```yaml
# Kyverno policy requiring attestation before deployment
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-model-attestation
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  rules:
  - name: attested-model-artifact
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: [Deployment]
    validate:
      message: Attestation required for model artifact
      pattern:
        metadata.annotations.cosign_attested: "true"
```

```rego
package kubernetes.admission

deny[{"msg": msg}] {
  input.request.kind.kind == "Deployment"
  not input.request.object.metadata.annotations["cosign_attested"] == "true"
  msg = "Model artifact must be attested with cosign before deployment"
}
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to enforce secure secret handling across multi-cloud clusters, using policy-as-code, and integrating cert-manager with GitOps pipelines.

## Key Concepts
- Policy as code (Kyverno/OPA)
- cert-manager Certificate -> Secret flow
- ExternalSecret / SecretStore integration
- CI gating and canary verification

## Code Example
```yaml
# Kyverno policy (example)
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-inline-tls-and-enforce-secretref
spec:
  validationFailureAction: fail
  rules:
  - name: deny-inline-tls
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment", "StatefulSet"]
    validate:
      message: "TLS data must come from cert-manager SecretRef; do not inline certificates"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              volumes:
              - secret:
                  secretName: "?!*"
```

```rego
# OPA/ValidatingAdmissionPolicy (illustrative)
package kubernetes.admission

deny[{"msg":"inline certs not allowed"}] {
  input.request.kind.kind == "Deployment" or input.request.kind.kind == "StatefulSet"
  some i
  secret := input.request.object.spec.template.spec.volumes[i]
  secret.secretName != "" # ensure SecretRef used, not inline data
}
```

```yaml
# Failing manifest (inline cert example)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: tls-secret
type: kubernetes.io/tls
data:
  tls.crt: LS0tLS1CRUdJTiBDRVJUSUZJQ0FURS0tLS0t... # inline cert data
  tls.key: LS0tLS1CRUdJTiBSU0EgUFJ...
```

```yaml
# Passing manifest (SecretRef to cert-manager Secret)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      volumes:
      - name: tls
        secret:
          secretName: my-cert-manager-secret
```

```yaml
# CI validation steps (high level)
- lint manifests
- run policy gate (Kyverno/OPA) on PR
- validate that Deployment references cert-manager Secret (no inline data)
- run a quick canary test in a staging cluster
```

## Why This Is Asked
This tests practical security tooling integration and explains how to enforce image signing early.

## Key Concepts
- Image signing with cosign
- Manifest parsing to collect images
- CI integration (GitHub Actions) and local validation

## Code Example
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
PUBKEY=${COSIGN_PUBLIC_KEY:-cosign.pub}
for f in manifests/**/*.yaml; do
  images=$(yq e '.. | .image? // empty' "$f" 2>/dev/null)
  for img in $images; do
    cosign verify --key "$PUBKEY" "$img" || { echo "Unsigned: $img"; exit 1; }
  done
done
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Immutability of container images is a core security practice. This checks a tangible gating mechanism candidates can implement in a simple CI step.

## Key Concepts

- YAML manifest parsing
- Image digest pinning (immutable refs)
- Lightweight CI scripts in GitHub Actions
- Local verification parity with CI

## Code Example

```yaml
# .github/workflows/pin-digest.yml
name: Pin Image Digests
on:
  push:
    paths:
      - '**/*.yaml'
      - '**/*.yml'
jobs:
  digest_check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Install jq and yq
        run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y jq wget
      - name: Install yq
        run: wget -qO- https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/releases/download/v4.25.1/yq_linux_amd64 -O /usr/bin/yq && chmod +x /usr/bin/yq
      - name: Validate image digests
        run: |
          DIGESTED=$(yq -r '.. | .image? // empty' **/*.yaml **/*.yml | grep -v '^$' )
          if echo "$DIGESTED" | grep -vq '@sha256:'; then
            echo "Found image refs without digest:";
            echo "$DIGESTED"; exit 1;
          fi
          echo "All images pinned to digests."
```
